title: Aurora Over Texas
subtitle: GIC, Conservative Operations & Timing Holdover

brief.userPrompt: Tuesday 16 March 2027, Central Daylight Time (UTC minus 5). The exercise starts at 02:00 in the NLTO control room in Duluth (day shift supervisor Walter Nakamura comes on at 06:00; reliability engineer Dr. Imani Okeke, Transmission Operations Manager Gloria Banerjee, Communications Manager Tess Lindholm) with the Upper Midwest Reliability Coordinator (Shift Manager Hugo Villanueva). The state of the sun: an X-class flare on Monday evening (a brief radio blackout, R3) with a fast halo CME. SWPC issued a Geomagnetic Storm Watch for G3 (WATA50) at 22:30 Monday for Tuesday, and at 02:10 Tuesday its CME discussion gives an arrival window of 11:00 to 17:00 CDT. The Kp record of a real severe storm is replayed (case data) and shifted to the dates here. Timeline: 13:24 sudden impulse detected at the solar wind monitor (WARSUD); 14:06 Kp 7 observed (G3 alert); 15:10 Kp 8 (G4); a K-index warning for Kp 8 or greater was issued at 14:40; 17:47 Kp 9 (G5) with the highest neutral current of 168 amperes at the Iron Range T2 autotransformer; Kp returns to 4 by 23:00 Tuesday evening; the exercise ends Wednesday morning with termination of the procedure. Pressure points: apply NLTO-OP-31 conditions before the Kp condition is reached (Condition 1 on the watch, Condition 2 on the Kp 6 warning, Condition 3 on Kp 7 or 75 amperes, Condition 4 on Kp 8 or 150 amperes), recording the basis and the time; defer 6 planned 345 kV outages (one is a 14-hour transformer replacement at Hartley); bring the Cloquet static var compensator and capacitor banks on line; reduce transfers across the Arrowhead (1,000 MW limit) and North Shore (600 MW limit) interfaces by 10 percent then another 10 percent; the Iron Range T2 gas alarm and a hot-spot reading 108 C force the Manager on call to decide on removing the transformer from service while the spare is at Hartley; 3 of the 14 substation GPS clocks lose lock after 16:00 and the control room must switch time sources and declare holdover; the 14 entities must be told within 60 minutes each time (UMRC, six neighboring TOPs, Taconite Ridge, Lake Superior Hydro, Baraga Wind Farm, the Minnesota duty officer, Mesabi Taconite Works, Duluth Harbor Terminal, the NLTO timing team and an executive on call); the RC runs hourly calls and raises its level from Alert to Warning to Emergency; a line trip at 16:20 on a 345 kV line and a relay misoperation at Hartley complicate the picture; social posts claim a nationwide blackout and a grid attack and aurora is seen as far south as Texas; the Mesabi Taconite Works duty manager asks whether to shut a furnace; the exercise should not give engineering advice about protection settings. Decisions the exercise should record: applying and terminating the operating procedure, dissemination to entities, grid operating actions (reduce transfers, bring reactive resources on line, defer outages), holdover and time source switches, customer notices, public messages. The SimCell plays NOAA SWPC forecasters, the reliability coordinator, neighboring operators, generator operators, the state duty officer, Mesabi Taconite Works, the transformer manufacturer's engineer, reporters and the public.
constraints: Every NLTO email address uses the exercise domain nlto-grid.example; the reliability coordinator uses umrc-grid.example; customers and neighbors use fictional domains; never a real utility, grid operator or newspaper domain.

Space weather products follow the SWPC layout and message codes (WATA, WARK, ALTK, WARSUD) with UTC times and are marked as exercise products; G levels map to Kp as G1 5, G2 6, G3 7, G4 8, G5 9; local times are Central Daylight Time; messages do not give engineering advice about protection settings.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; NOAA SWPC, neighboring operators, generator owners, the state duty officer, customers, the transformer manufacturer, reporters and the public are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Acting on the forecast before the Kp arrives, keeping a stressed 345 kV system and its transformers in service, and making sure NLTO, the RC, NOAA and the state give the same numbers to entities and the public.
overview.threat: An X-class flare on Monday evening, 15 March 2027, caused a brief R3 radio blackout and launched a fast halo CME. At 22:30 CDT Monday, before STARTEX, SWPC issued a G3 Geomagnetic Storm Watch (WATA50) for Tuesday. At 02:10 CDT Tuesday its CME discussion gives an arrival window of 11:00 to 17:00 CDT. The CME arrives as a sudden impulse at 13:24 CDT (WARSUD). Kp 7 (G3) is observed at 14:06, the Kp 8 or greater warning is issued at 14:40, Kp 8 (G4) arrives at 15:10 and Kp 9 (G5) at 17:47. Geomagnetically induced currents flow in the 345/230 kV autotransformers of the Northern Lakes Transmission Operations network, the reactive power swings across the Arrowhead and North Shore interfaces, and GNSS timing at the substations degrades. The storm data are a replay of the Kp record from a real severe storm (case data) shifted to these dates. All SWPC products are exercise products, with times in UTC.
overview.operationalImpact:
The exercise starts at 02:00 CDT Tuesday in the Duluth control room with the night shift, after the watch has been issued. Day shift supervisor Walter Nakamura comes on at 06:00. The narrative moves in time jumps from the early-morning watch through the afternoon storm to the end of the procedure on Wednesday morning.

Before arrival, operators must apply Condition 1 and then Condition 2 ahead of the Kp they trigger on, recording the basis and the time. They must also defer six planned 345 kV outages, including a 14-hour transformer replacement at Hartley, and bring the Cloquet static var compensator and the Iron Range and Hartley capacitor banks on line.

After the impulse:
- Neutral-current alarms climb on the EMS display, and the two transfer cuts follow: transfers across the Arrowhead (1,000 MW limit) and North Shore (600 MW limit) interfaces are cut by 10 percent and then by another 10 percent.
- A 345 kV line trips at 16:20 and a relay misoperates at Hartley, so the picture on the one-line becomes unclear.
- After 16:00, three substation GPS clocks lose lock. PMU data on the wide-area screen become suspect until the supervisor switches time sources and declares holdover.
- At 17:47 the Iron Range T2 autotransformer reaches 168 amperes neutral current, with a gas alarm and a 108 C hot-spot reading. Transmission Operations Manager Gloria Banerjee must decide whether to remove it from service, knowing the only spare is stored at Hartley. Reliability engineer Dr. Imani Okeke advises, and the SimCell transformer manufacturer's engineer is on the phone.

Each condition change starts a 60-minute clock for notifying 14 entities. The UMRC (Shift Manager Hugo Villanueva) raises its level from Alert to Warning to Emergency and runs hourly calls, then calls every 30 minutes. The Mesabi Taconite Works duty manager calls to ask whether to shut a furnace. Reporters call about aurora seen as far south as Texas. Communications Manager Tess Lindholm faces social posts claiming a nationwide blackout and a grid attack. Kp falls to 4 by 23:00, and the exercise ends Wednesday morning when the procedure is terminated. The exercise gives no engineering advice on protection settings.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to apply NGDOP Conditions 1 through 4 ahead of the Kp they trigger on when SWPC lead time allows, including deferring the six planned 345 kV outages and the Hartley transformer replacement, bringing the Cloquet SVC and the Iron Range and Hartley capacitor banks on line, and logging the basis and time of each condition change and of the termination.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to decide whether to remove the Iron Range T2 autotransformer from service at 168 A neutral current with a gas alarm and a 108 C hot-spot reading, weighing the loss of the only spare stored at Hartley against system security and agreeing the related transfer cuts on the Arrowhead and North Shore interfaces with the UMRC.

objectives.name: Technical Analysis
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to keep an accurate operating picture after the 16:20 line trip, the Hartley relay misoperation and the loss of lock at three substation GPS clocks, by identifying suspect PMU data, switching to the backup network time source and declaring holdover within the 24-hour holdover limit.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to notify all 14 NGDOP entities within 60 minutes of each condition change and to issue public statements under the NLTO Communications Plan that match the UMRC and SWPC on G level and duration, while answering the Mesabi Taconite Works furnace question and correcting posts that claim a nationwide blackout or a grid attack.

roles.name: Control Room Shift Supervisor
roles.team: Team A: Control Room Shift Supervisor
roles.description: Owns the NGDOP operating procedure in the Duluth control room: declares each condition, takes its actions, keeps the log, starts each 60-minute notification clock and proposes when to end the procedure.
standingOrders: Act Early: when SWPC gives lead time, apply the next condition's actions before the Kp is observed and log the product, the time and the reason.
Verify the Picture: if the one-line, the neutral-current alarms and the PMU screen disagree, treat the data as suspect until you have checked them and say so on the RC call.
Hold Steady: do not switch to restore a tripped line in Condition 3 or higher unless the RC agrees, even when the field crew is ready.
Count the Clock: each condition change starts a 60-minute clock for all 14 entities, so assign someone to the binder list before you work the next alarm.

roles.name: Reliability Engineer
roles.description: Owns the GIC and transformer risk picture, including neutral-current trends, transformer thermal and gas indications, contingency analysis and the post-event review of the Hartley relay misoperation.
standingOrders: Advise, Don't Guess: give the Manager the evidence (neutral current, hot-spot, gas alarm, trend) and its uncertainty, not a reassuring number.
Respect the Spare: there is only one spare and it is at Hartley, so frame every transformer recommendation as the cost of losing the unit against the cost of losing the spare.
Stay in Lane: the vendor's engineer and the RC give advice, but NLTO's decision on its own equipment stays with NLTO, and the exercise makes no protection-setting changes on the fly.

roles.name: Transmission Operations Manager
roles.description: Owns the high-consequence decisions: deferring outages including the Hartley replacement, approving transfer cuts and extra reserve, removing the Iron Range T2 autotransformer and escalating to the Director of System Operations and the executive on call.
standingOrders: Equipment Survives the Storm: a damaged autotransformer takes months to replace, while a transfer cut can be undone in hours.
Decide on the Record: make the T2 decision with the reliability engineer present, state the trigger you used and log it, and do not wait for certainty that will not come.
Coordinate, Don't Freelance: agree further transfer cuts with the UMRC and ask the state duty officer for a call at Condition 4 before load-shed plan NLTO-OP-12 is ever needed.

roles.name: Communications Manager
roles.description: Owns NLTO's public voice: the condition-based statements in the Communications Plan, the media briefings with the Director of System Operations, and the answers to rumors of a nationwide blackout or a grid attack.
standingOrders: Impacts, Not Physics: say what NLTO is doing and what customers should expect, quote the SWPC product by time and level, and link to SWPC.
Never Beat SWPC: do not give an end time earlier than SWPC's, and do not speak for NOAA or for the RC's wide-area operations.

Truth Over Reassurance: correct the blackout and attack claims quickly, but only with facts the control room has confirmed, and keep the G level and duration the same as the UMRC and the state duty officer give.

roles.name: UMRC Shift Manager (Reliability Coordinator Shift Manager)
roles.team: Team E: Reliability Coordinator Shift Manager
roles.description: Owns the wide-area GMD picture under UGFNWC: issues the Alert, Warning and Emergency notices, runs the hourly and then 30-minute conference bridge, and directs interface transfer reductions, redispatch and the sharing of reactive reserves.
standingOrders: Fifteen Minutes: send each RC notice to the TOP, generator owner and neighbor lists within 15 minutes of the SWPC product, with the serial number, UTC and Central times and the next call time.
Escalate on Evidence: raise to Emergency when two TOPs report neutral currents above their thresholds or voltage problems, and tell the state emergency management agencies then.
Not Their Relays: direct transfers, redispatch and outage schedules, but never a TOP's protection settings.

roles.name: Substation and Timing Engineer (NLTO Fiber and Telecommunications Timing Team)
roles.team: Team F: Substation and Timing Engineer
roles.description: Owns the GPS-disciplined substation clocks, the 24-hour holdover clocks, the backup network time source over the fiber ring at Duluth and the timing alarms that feed protection and the PMUs.
standingOrders: Flag Before You Fix: tell the supervisor at once which substations lost lock and which PMU feeds are now suspect, before you start the failover.
Know the Holdover Clock: record when each site entered holdover and track it against the 24-hour limit, and do not declare GPS restored until lock is stable.
One Change at a Time: switch time sources site by site with the control room's agreement, never in the middle of a switching operation or a relay event review.

phases.title: The Overnight Watch
phases.goal: Tests whether the night and day shifts apply NGDOP Condition 1, then Condition 2, on the SWPC forecast before any Kp is observed. It also tests whether they defer the planned 345 kV work, the Hartley transformer replacement among it, while the CME arrival time is still uncertain by hours.
beats: (02:10) The exercise SWPC CME discussion gives an arrival window of 11:00 to 17:00 CDT, on top of the WATA50 G3 watch issued at 22:30 Monday. The UMRC Alert notice arrives with its message code, serial number, times in UTC and Central and the next call time. Players should apply NGDOP 4 Condition 1 and log the code, time and basis as NGDOP 3 requires: confirm the GIC monitors report, confirm the Section 6 contact list for the 14 entities and check where the spare transformer is stored at Hartley.

Noise item: a SUMX01 flare summary and a late R3 radio-blackout report from Monday evening arrive in the shift supervisor's inbox. They have no grid action attached and must not be mistaken for a new trigger. Also, the Iron Range GIC monitor misses one polling cycle and comes back on its own, which tests the Condition 1 check that the monitors report.

(06:00) Walter Nakamura takes over the day shift. The outage coordinator asks whether the six planned 345 kV outages still go ahead today, including the 14-hour Hartley transformer replacement crew already on site. The Mesabi Taconite Works duty manager asks whether to change today's production schedule.

(09:30) With the window opening at 11:00, players weigh moving to NGDOP 4 Condition 2 actions ahead of the Kp 6 trigger. The actions are: energize the Cloquet SVC (±200 MVAR) and the Iron Range (2 x 100 MVAR) and Hartley (2 x 75 MVAR) capacitor banks before the storm, add the second shift supervisor and Dr. Imani Okeke to the control room, and record the basis for acting early.

Each condition change starts the 60-minute clock to notify the 14 entities under NGDOP 6. Tess Lindholm drafts the first Condition 1/2 holding statement under the NLTO Communications Plan, Section 3, quoting the G3 level and the duration exactly as SWPC and the UMRC give them.

phases.title: Shock Arrival
phases.goal: Tests whether the control room recognizes the sudden impulse and moves quickly through Conditions 2, 3 and 4 as the Kp and neutral-current triggers are crossed. It also tests whether the transfer cuts on the Arrowhead and North Shore interfaces are agreed with the UMRC and the 14 entities are kept informed.
beats: Time jump to 13:24 CDT: an exercise WARSUD sudden-impulse warning sounds the control room alarm. The UMRC raises its level to Warning, applies the second condition and starts hourly calls. Neutral-current values climb on the EMS GIC display. Players confirm Condition 2 is fully in place and log the time.

(14:06) Kp 7 (G3) is observed and neutral current passes 75 A at a monitored 345/230 kV transformer, with a reactive swing of more than 150 MVAR. Players should apply NGDOP 4 Condition 3: cut transfers 10 percent on the Arrowhead (1,000 MW limit) and North Shore (600 MW limit) interfaces, add 200 MW of operating reserve, hold the line outages, and notify the generator operators and large customers. Visual for the room: a screenshot of the EMS neutral-current trend.
Red herring: Lakeshore Power Cooperative reports a 'tripped 345 kV tie' on the North Shore interface. A callback shows it was a planned outage of theirs, logged the week before, and not a GIC trip.

(14:40–15:10) The exercise WARK08 (Kp 8 or greater) warning arrives, followed by Kp 8 (G4) observed. Players should apply NGDOP 4 Condition 4: a further 10 percent transfer cut agreed with the UMRC, consideration of extra generation near the load, a call to the Minnesota Department of Public Safety duty officer, and NLTO-OP-12 kept ready. The UMRC raises its level to Emergency under UGFNWC 4 and moves to calls every 30 minutes. The UGFNWC 5 acknowledgment check finds one generator owner, the Baraga Wind Farm, has not acknowledged within 30 minutes.
Reporters call about aurora seen as far south as Texas, and one has a 16:00 deadline. Tess Lindholm must match the G4 level and the hours-to-a-day duration that SWPC and the UMRC are giving.

phases.title: Iron Range T2 Decision
phases.goal: Tests whether the team keeps an accurate operating picture through a line trip, a relay misoperation and the loss of GPS timing. It also tests whether Gloria Banerjee makes and records the decision on removing the Iron Range T2 autotransformer from service, weighing the only spare against system security.
beats: After 16:00, three substation GPS clocks lose lock and PMU phase angles on the wide-area screen drift and become suspect. The Substation and Timing Engineer must identify the affected PMUs, switch to the backup network time source under NGDOP 7 and declare holdover. Players log the start time against the 24-hour holdover limit.

(16:20) A 345 kV line trips and a relay misoperates at Hartley, so the one-line picture is unclear. Players must work out what actually opened without trusting the suspect PMU data. Under NGDOP 4 Condition 3, they must not switch to restore the line unless the UMRC agrees.

(17:47) Kp 9 (G5) is observed. The Iron Range T2 autotransformer reaches 168 A neutral current, with a gas alarm and a 108 C hot-spot reading. THE DECISION POINT: if T2 is removed from service, the Arrowhead and North Shore transfer limits drop further, and if it fails, the only replacement is the spare stored at Hartley. If T2 is kept in service, the transformer itself may be damaged. Dr. Imani Okeke advises, the SimCell manufacturer's engineer is on the phone, and the related transfer cuts must be agreed with Hugo Villanueva at the UMRC. The decision is about operations only; the exercise gives no advice on protection settings.
The Mesabi Taconite Works duty manager calls back asking whether to shut a furnace now. Players must answer within what NLTO knows and is allowed to say, and must not promise grid conditions.

Social posts claim a nationwide blackout and a grid attack. Tess Lindholm must issue a correction under the NLTO Communications Plan, Section 3, that matches SWPC and the UMRC on G5 and the expected duration. Meanwhile the 60-minute NGDOP 6 notice for Condition 4 and the Kp 9 escalation must reach all 14 entities, including the NLTO fiber and telecommunications timing team and the executive on call.

phases.title: Termination and Restoration
phases.goal: Tests whether the team meets the termination conditions in UGFNWC 8 before ending the procedure, plans a phased return of deferred work and the spare-transformer logistics, and closes notifications and post-event reporting with complete logs.
beats: Time jump to 23:00 CDT: Kp has fallen to 4. Players review the Iron Range T2 condition and the Hartley relay misoperation. They set restoration priorities: the 16:20 line (restored only with UMRC agreement), the Iron Range T2 status, and the order for bringing the six deferred 345 kV outages back.

Hurdle: the Hartley spare transformer cannot move before a heavy-haul permit and a crane are available days from now, so the Hartley replacement must be rescheduled around it. At the same time, two of the three GPS clocks will not reacquire lock and holdover continues toward the 24-hour limit. The timing engineer has to plan for this.

Wednesday morning: SWPC warnings have expired and Kp has been 4 or lower for 3 hours. The UMRC proposes ending the warning, and NLTO must agree as one of the TOPs. Players then terminate the NGDOP procedure and log the time and basis. The 60-minute NGDOP 6 termination notice goes to all 14 entities, and the UGFNWC 5 check confirms how many entities were told.

The UMRC sends the termination message and the UGFNWC 8 post-event data request. NLTO prepares its short report: highest neutral current (168 A at Iron Range T2), actions taken and times. Tess Lindholm issues a final 'storm over' statement and the Minnesota Department of Public Safety duty officer is updated. ENDEX.

objectiveCapabilities.why: Players must apply NGDOP Conditions 1 through 4 ahead of the Kp that triggers them when SWPC gives lead time. Each condition change, and the termination, has to be logged with its basis and agreed with the UMRC under the RC notification levels.

The condition actions are changes to the grid itself: deferring the six 345 kV outages and the Hartley transformer replacement, and bringing the Cloquet SVC and the Iron Range and Hartley capacitor banks on line.
The decision on the Iron Range T2 autotransformer (168 A, gas alarm, 108 C hot-spot) weighs protecting a critical grid asset against using the only spare at Hartley and keeping the system secure.
Removing T2 depends on agreeing the reduced Arrowhead and North Shore transfer schedules and the redispatch with the UMRC Shift Manager on the bridge before the unit is opened.

After the 16:20 trip, the Hartley relay misoperation and the GPS loss of lock, the room has to keep an accurate operating picture. That means checking neutral currents, breaker status and suspect PMU data before acting.
Losing lock at three substation clocks calls for the NGDOP 7 switch to the backup network time source and a holdover declaration within the 24-hour holdover limit.
All 14 NGDOP entities, the generator operators, the large customers and the state duty officer must be told at each condition change and at termination, and the UMRC notices must reach them on time.

hotwash.methodDescription: 3-Up, 3-Down asks the room for three things that went well and three things that broke or failed during the exercise. Go around the room one team at a time (control room, reliability engineering, communications, management) so every team gets a turn, and write each item on the whiteboard in two columns before you start the discussion questions.

questions.text: You had the G3 Watch from Monday night, the 02:10 CME discussion with an 11:00–17:00 arrival window, and the 13:24 sudden impulse, but Kp 7 wasn't observed until 14:06. NGDOP 4 says to take a condition's actions before the condition is reached when SWPC gives lead time. At what time did you actually defer the six 345 kV outages and the Hartley transformer replacement, and bring the Cloquet SVC and the Iron Range and Hartley capacitor banks on line? Did you act on the forecast, or wait for the Kp to show up before you moved? Which condition change has no logged time or basis, and what stopped you writing it down?

At 17:47 (I-12), Iron Range T2 read 168 A neutral current with an H2 gas alarm and a 108 C hot spot. The manufacturer said it was 'the pattern we see before winding damage' but couldn't confirm it without an oil sample. Your only spare was at Hartley, where 345-1 was out and the relay status was unclear. Did you remove T2 or keep it in service, and how long did the decision take? Did the reliability engineer's view of the transformer and the Shift Manager's view of system security reach the same answer, or did one side overrule the other? Did UMRC have your new Arrowhead (540 MW) and North Shore (320 MW) schedules, and the Taconite Ridge gas units on 20 minutes' notice, before anyone opened a breaker? What information would have let you make the call faster?

After the 16:20 line trip, the Hartley relay misoperation and the loss of lock at three substation GPS clocks, when did you stop trusting the PMU data and the timestamps in front of you? Who spotted that the data were suspect, and how was that passed to the operators: as evidence that changed the operating picture, or as a ticket for someone to look at later? When did you switch to the backup network time source and declare holdover, and did everyone know the 24-hour holdover limit and when that clock started?

At 15:44 (I-06b), the UMRC acknowledgment report showed Baraga Wind Farm had not acknowledged, and your own Condition 4 tally had 12 of 14 entities ticked, with Baraga and Duluth Harbor Terminal blank and the 60-minute clock running out at 16:10. Baraga said they never saw the Warning or the Emergency. How did you find the gap: by checking actively, or because UMRC's report pointed it out? What should the two entities have been doing for the storm while they were in the dark? Separately, Mesabi called at 07:35 and again at 17:30 (I-10b) wanting a straight answer about the indurating furnace. Did anyone actually keep them posted as promised that morning, and what did you tell them you could and couldn't guarantee?

At 07:55 (I-03b), before you knew how big the storm would get, Northland 6 asked whether the lights would go out in Duluth, while a post claiming a G5 storm at noon had 2,300 shares. What did you tell the public then? At 17:50–17:53 (I-12b), G5 was real, a post claimed a nationwide blackout, another called the 16:20 Hartley trip a cyberattack, and MN HSEM's draft said 'G4, ending by 22:00 CDT.' Did your statement match SWPC and UMRC on the G level and on duration (storms last from several hours to a day)? Did you correct HSEM's draft, and how did you answer the cyberattack claim without guessing? When did you first bring in the state emergency management duty officer, as NGDOP Condition 4 calls for, and did you wait too long?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) forecaster on duty, Boulder, Colorado (the weather / hazard authority)
simcellScripts.trigger: A player calls or emails SWPC to ask when the CME will arrive, how bad it will get, or when the storm will end (most likely after I-01, I-03, I-07 or I-15).
hardQuestions: "Our discussion gives 1600 to 2200 UTC for arrival, uncertain by several hours. I can't narrow that for you. What decision are you trying to make, and what's your procedure's trigger?"
"You're asking me if it's G3 or G4 right now. Which product are you reading? Give me the message code and serial number. I won't confirm a level off a news screenshot."
"We forecast the space weather. Whether your transformers or relays can take it is your engineering call. I can't advise on that."
"'When does it end' isn't something I can promise. WARK08 is valid to 0300 UTC, and storms run hours to a day. Are you quoting our valid times or making up an end time for the public?"
concessions: Once the player quotes a specific product by code and serial, the forecaster restates its valid times in UTC and the scale level it carries.

If the player says the decision depends on lead time, the forecaster explains that a K-index 7 warning may come only 30 to 90 minutes before the Kp is observed and that a sudden impulse means the main storm may follow within minutes to hours. This supports acting on the watch.

In Phase 4, if the player asks about end conditions rather than an all-clear, the forecaster confirms that no geomagnetic warning is active after WARK05 expires. The forecaster says there is no second CME in the current discussion and that products will be issued if that changes.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Minnesota Department of Public Safety, Homeland Security and Emergency Management (HSEM) duty officer (651-555-0140. The same character also passes on questions from St. Louis County / City of Duluth emergency management, the county and city emergency management agency.
simcellScripts.trigger: NLTO notifies HSEM at Condition 4 (NGDOP 4 asks for a call with the state duty officer), or a player calls back about the HSEM draft public messages in I-07, I-12b or I-16b.
hardQuestions: "My 18:30 update says 'Severe (G4), expected to end by 22:00.' The county wants to know if they should open warming centers tonight. Are any Minnesotans without power, yes or no, and how many?"
"The UMRC told me Emergency at 15:14. Your notice says Condition 4. My governor's office doesn't know what either means. Give me one sentence a county EM can read out."
"Social media is saying Hartley was a cyberattack. Are you telling me it wasn't? On what basis? If you won't put that in writing, I can't either."
"I need your wording by 05:45 or my 06:00 update goes out as drafted. Who signed off on what you're giving me?"
concessions: If NLTO sends written wording that matches the UMRC level and the current SWPC product (G level, duration stated as 'several hours to a day', outage count), HSEM uses NLTO's wording and drops its own end time.
If NLTO gives a named contact and a next-update time, HSEM agrees to hold county inquiries and route them through that contact.

If NLTO confirms in writing that there are no customer outages, HSEM's 06:00 update says 'storm ended; no customer outages reported in the NLTO footprint'. It names NLTO as the source and makes no claim about the cause of the Hartley trip.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Mesabi Taconite Works duty manager Peter Lindgren (218-555-0127 (directly connected industrial customer)
simcellScripts.trigger: I-02b (morning call) or I-10b (17:30 call), or any time NLTO calls Mesabi with a condition notice under the Communications Plan Section 4.
hardQuestions: "Yes or no: will you guarantee me power through 17:00? I've got 180 MW of pellet lines and an indurating furnace that takes eight hours to bring back cold."
"You said you'd keep me posted. My voltage blinked at 16:20 and I heard it from my electrician, not you. Why?"
"If I take 90 MW off and you black me out anyway, I've lost a day of pellets. What exactly are you asking me to do, and who's paying for it?"
"Is it getting worse or better? Give me a number I can tell my plant manager in fifteen minutes."
concessions: If NLTO states the current condition and what NLTO has done, and asks Mesabi to keep power factor correction in service and report any load change (the Communications Plan Section 4 notice), Mesabi agrees and gives a direct callback number for the shift lead.
If NLTO gives a firm time for its next call and keeps to it, Mesabi holds off on a furnace decision until that call.
Mesabi does not accept a guarantee or an instruction to shut the furnace. If NLTO declines to give either and explains the risk honestly, Mesabi makes its own business call and says so on the record.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Transformer manufacturer field service engineer for the Iron Range T2 single-phase large-core bank (SimCell, on speakerphone)
simcellScripts.trigger: I-12 at 17:47, or any time the Reliability Engineer or Manager calls the manufacturer about T2's neutral current, gas alarm or hot-spot temperature, or about moving the Hartley spare.
hardQuestions: "Before I say anything: what's the serial number, what's your service agreement or ticket number, and who's authorizing this call on your side?"
"Hydrogen rising at 108 C under DC bias is the pattern we see before winding damage. Do you have a trend of the DGA and the hot spot, with times, or just the alarm? Has anyone drawn an oil sample?"
"I can't tell you it's damaged without an oil sample, and I won't tell you to keep it in or take it out. The call is yours. Who's making it?"
"If it fails, a new unit is 14 to 18 months out. Your spare's at Hartley. Do you have a heavy-haul permit and a crane, or is that a week away?"
concessions: If NLTO gives a ticket number and a named authorizing manager, the engineer opens a priority case and agrees to review the DGA and temperature trend once it is sent in writing.
If NLTO draws an oil sample and logs the time, the engineer commits to interpreting the lab result in the morning and advising on returning the unit to service.
With a signed service request, the engineer will confirm the spare's nameplate compatibility and send rigging and transport notes for the Hartley spare.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Northland 6 News assignment desk / producer (555-0147). Also used for the Gulf Coast Herald reporter calling from Texas.
simcellScripts.trigger: I-03b, I-07 or I-16b, or the Communications Manager calls back a media slip.
hardQuestions: "We go live at 11:58. Are the lights going out in Duluth today, yes or no?"
"People in San Antonio are filming aurora and saying Minnesota's grid is down. How many of your customers are out right now? I file at 16:00. I'll say NLTO didn't respond if I don't hear back."
"The state's draft says G3 ending at 18:00, and the SWPC site says G4. Which is it? And was Hartley a hack, yes or no?"
"Can I get someone on camera at 06:10? A name and a title, not a spokesperson email."
concessions: If the Communications Manager gives a short, attributable statement that names the condition, what NLTO has done, and a next-update time before the deadline, the outlet runs NLTO's quote rather than the social posts.
If NLTO sends the same G level and wording as the state (HSEM) and the current SWPC product, the producer drops the 'conflicting reports' angle.
If NLTO commits to the 06:10 live slot with a named spokesperson, the producer gives the questions in advance.

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. Players' decisions and the gaps they find are used to improve NLTO and UMRC plans, not to grade individuals.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. All SWPC products, EMS alarms and neutral-current readings are exercise data and are treated as real for play.
Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures, including NGDOP, UGFNWC and the NLTO Communications Plan. Where a plan is silent, players state what they would do and why.
Players have only the information in the module narrative and the injects delivered so far. They do not have knowledge of later events, causes or outcomes.

Players act within the authority of their real-world role. The UMRC Shift Manager speaks for the reliability coordinator, and the Transmission Operations Manager decides on removing transformers from service.
artificialities: Each module starts with a time jump. Scenario time moves from 02:00 CDT Tuesday to 06:00 CDT Wednesday in four one-hour modules, and some injects inside a module also move the narrative clock forward.

The SimCell plays everyone outside the room. This includes NOAA SWPC forecasters, the Minnesota HSEM duty officer, the neighboring TOPs, generator desks, Mesabi Taconite Works, the Hartley crew, vendors, contractors, the media and members of the public.

The EMS, SCADA, PMU wide-area screen, GNSS timing monitor, UMRC Notification System and entity conference bridge are named as they appear in the plans but are not touched. All alarms, displays and messages arrive on paper or on the projected screen.
No real switching, notifications, public posts or media statements are made. Players describe the action, its time and who they tell, and the facilitator records it.
The geomagnetic storm, the CME, all SWPC message codes and serial numbers, and the neighboring utilities are fictional and created for this exercise.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 1: The Overnight Watch (exercise clock 0:00–1:00; scenario 02:00 to about 11:30 CDT, Tuesday 16 March 2027)**

It is 02:00 CDT in the NLTO primary control room in Duluth. One Control Room Shift Supervisor is on the desk, and the reliability engineer is on call from home. Load is 2,240 MW. Arrowhead imports are 610 MW against a 1,000 MW limit, and North Shore imports are 340 MW against 600 MW. All 345 kV lines are in service. The Cloquet SVC and the Iron Range and Hartley capacitor banks are off line. All 14 substation GPS clocks are locked. The log shows that an SWPC G3 Geomagnetic Storm Watch (WATA50) for today arrived at 22:30 CDT Monday. It was logged, and no other action was taken.

At 02:10 the alarm rings for an SWPC CME discussion. A fast halo CME from an X2.1 flare is expected between 1600 and 2200 UTC (11:00–17:00 CDT). The arrival window is uncertain by several hours. G3 is likely, with a chance of G4. Six planned 345 kV outages are booked for today, including the 14-hour Hartley AT-1 replacement with its crew and crane already on site. A GPS clock firmware push is also scheduled for 10:00. The real-time Kp is quiet.
keyIssues: Whether a G3 watch logged at 22:30 should already have triggered Condition 1, and when to move to Condition 2 on forecast rather than on observed Kp.
A go/no-go on the Hartley AT-1 replacement and five other 345 kV outages, with real standby costs, while the CME arrival time is uncertain by hours.
Whether to let a vendor restart GPS clocks at four substations on the day of a forecast storm.
Confirming that GIC monitors report after a communications failure at Iron Range AT2.
Giving entities, Mesabi Taconite Works and the media consistent numbers when a viral post claims G5 and a grid collapse lasting days.

It is 13:24 CDT. Kp has stayed at 3 through the morning, and day load is 2,860 MW. Arrowhead imports are 780 MW against 1,000 MW, and North Shore imports are 470 MW against 600 MW. The control room alarm has just sounded for an SWPC WARSUD message: a geomagnetic sudden impulse is expected from 1835 UTC, after shock passage was observed at 1817 UTC. **Module 3: Iron Range T2 Decision (exercise clock 2:00–3:00; scenario 16:00 to about 17:55 CDT, Tuesday 16 March 2027)**

It is 16:00 CDT. Kp 8 (G4, Severe) has held since 15:10, and the SWPC K-index warning is valid until 22:00 CDT. NLTO is in Condition 4. Both transfer cuts were agreed on the UMRC bridge: Arrowhead is now 620 MW and North Shore 375 MW. Operating reserve is up by 200 MW, and the Cloquet SVC and the Iron Range and Hartley capacitor banks are on line. All six planned 345 kV outages are deferred, and the Hartley AT-1 crew is standing by in the Hartley yard.

Neutral currents are Iron Range AT2 146 A, Hartley AT1 118 A and Cloquet AT1 71 A, and the saw-tooth is getting steeper. Load is 2,880 MW and climbing toward the evening peak. All 14 entities have now been notified of Condition 4. The UMRC is at Emergency, with calls every 30 minutes and the next at 16:30. From here the room has to defend the system it has.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 4: Termination and Restoration (exercise clock 3:00–4:00; scenario 23:00 CDT Tuesday 16 March to about 06:00 CDT Wednesday 17 March 2027)**

It is 23:00 CDT. Kp peaked at 9 (G5, Extreme) at 17:47. It fell to 7 by 20:00 and 5 by 21:00, and the real-time estimate now reads 4. The K-index 8 warning expired at 22:00 CDT. SWPC has since issued a K-index 5 persistence warning valid until 01:00 CDT. Neutral currents are Hartley AT1 14 A, Cloquet AT1 6 A, and all others below 10 A. Iron Range T2 is in the state the Manager chose at 17:47.

Line Hartley–Iron Range 345-1 has been open since 16:20. Breaker 3H22 is confirmed closed and 345-2 is carrying load, but no one has explained the 21 Z1 relay target. The Hartley AT-1 crew went home at 20:00. Arrowhead and North Shore remain on the reduced schedules agreed on the UMRC bridge, and load is 2,410 MW. The UMRC is still at Emergency, with the next call at 23:30. The storm is past its peak. The room now has to decide what comes back first and show when the event is over.
keyIssues: Showing that every NGDOP termination condition is met, including neutral currents below 25 A for 3 hours, before ending the procedure.
Setting the order in which deferred work returns: line 345-1, the six 345 kV outages, Iron Range T2 and the Hartley spare logistics.
Managing GPS clocks still in holdover against the 24-hour limit.
Closing termination notices to all 14 entities and completing the post-event report.
Giving a final public message, matched with the state, on outages, the end of the storm and rumors of a second CME.
